mainTopic: Freeing slaves: שמואל's prohibition and its מצוה exception, and רב's ruling that הקדש or הפקר frees a slave
overview: The amud opens at the end of a proof: a woman who was half-slave and half-free was being treated promiscuously, so the court forced her master to free her. The גמרא rejects this as a proof about a regular maidservant, since she can be married to the master's slave. It then returns to שמואל's rule that freeing a slave breaks a מצות עשה. רבי אליעזר freed his slave to complete a מנין, and the גמרא shows this was allowed only because it was for a מצוה, since רבי אליעזר holds that keeping slaves is a חובה. רבה adds that freeing slaves is one of three habits that make homeowners lose their wealth. Next comes רב's ruling that one who is מקדיש his slave, or makes him הפקר, sets him free, though the slave still needs a גט שחרור. The גמרא defends the הקדש ruling against several sources, and the amud ends with a new challenge from a ברייתא that says devoting a slave means devoting only his value.

steps.title: The court forced a master to free a half-free woman
steps.stepSummary: The proof ends: the court forced the master of a half-slave, half-free woman to free her, because people were treating her promiscuously.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court forced her master to free her completely. רב נחמן בר יצחק explained why: people were treating her as if she were ownerless and sinning with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that a master may be pushed to free a slave so that people stop sinning with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who is half שפחה and half בת חורין. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that she was freed because people were sinning with her. This seems to show that stopping sin is a good enough reason to free a slave, even with שמואל's rule against freeing slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: they forced (the court made him do it)
treating her like ownerless property, meaning people sinned with her freely

phrases.english: and they forced her master
and he made her a free woman.
And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They treated her like ownerless property!
phrases.notes: Meaning men were sinning with her freely, and that's why he was made to free her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָפוּ אֶת רַבָּהּ וַעֲשָׂאָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That a master may be made to free a slave to stop people from sinning with her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the half-free woman whose master was forced to free her, as explained by רב נחמן בר יצחק.

steps.title: The half-free woman's case is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the half-free woman cannot marry anyone, but a regular maidservant can be married to the master's slave, who will guard her.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare the two? There, she cannot marry a slave and she cannot marry a free man, so freeing her is the only fix. Here, the master can give her to his own slave, and he will guard her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof and says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A half-free woman is stuck: her slave half cannot marry a free man, and her free half cannot marry a slave. That is why freeing her was the only solution. A regular שפחה can be paired with the master's עבד, who will protect her, so there is no need to free her.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are not alike)
she is fit for, allowed to marry
designates, assigns her as a partner

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying it is fine for people to sin with a regular maidservant. It is saying there is another way to stop it, so freeing her is not needed.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, she is not fit for a slave
phrases.notes: Her free half stops her from marrying a slave.

phrases.english: and she is not fit for a free man;
phrases.notes: Her slave half stops her from marrying a free man.

phrases.english: here, it is possible for him to assign her to his slave,
and he will guard her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the half-free woman and a regular maidservant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The half-free woman had no other option, but a regular maidservant can be given to the master's slave for protection.
steps.whatToRemember: Freeing the half-free woman was a last resort, because she could not marry anyone. A regular maidservant has another solution, so her case cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: שמואל: freeing a slave breaks a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's rule that anyone who frees his slave breaks a מצות עשה, learned from the פסוק 'לעולם בהם תעבודו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main statement itself. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: anyone who frees his slave breaks a positive מצוה, because the פסוק says, 'You shall make them work for you forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to discuss שמואל's statement, which was quoted earlier, on its own terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us we are returning to a statement that was mentioned earlier in passing. שמואל reads 'לעולם' (forever) as a command to keep a Canaanite slave working all his life. So freeing him goes against an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the thing itself': returning to a statement quoted earlier

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule the whole surrounding discussion is about, and the next steps test it.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Anyone who frees his slave breaks a positive מצוה,
as it says: "You shall make them work for you forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to שמואל's rule itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freeing a Canaanite slave breaks the מצות עשה of 'לעולם בהם תעבודו'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר freed his slave to make a מנין
steps.stepSummary: A challenge to שמואל: רבי אליעזר found only nine men in shul, so he freed his slave to complete the ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges this: there was a story where רבי אליעזר came into a shul and did not find ten men. He freed his slave, and the slave made the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to go against שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If freeing a slave breaks an עשה, how could a great sage like רבי אליעזר do it? His action seems to show that freeing a slave is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: and made him complete the ten

phrases.english: They challenged: There was a story with Rabbi Eliezer
who entered a synagogue
and did not find ten,
and he freed his slave and had him complete the ten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that freeing a slave breaks an עשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר freed his slave, which suggests freeing a slave is allowed.

steps.title: Freeing a slave for a מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: Answer: freeing a slave in order to do a מצוה, like completing a מנין, is an exception to שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two words: freeing for the sake of a מצוה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule still stands in general. When freeing the slave makes a מצוה possible, like davening with a מנין, that is allowed. So רבי אליעזר's story does not prove that freeing a slave is allowed in every case.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: freeing a slave breaks an עשה ('לעולם בהם תעבודו'). Exception: freeing him to make a מצוה possible, like completing a מנין, is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel שמואל's rule. It only carves out an exception for a מצוה.

phrases.english: A מצוה is different.
phrases.notes: Davening with ten is a מצוה, and that's what makes freeing him allowed here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction: the case is an exception for a מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's action shows that freeing a slave is generally allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Freeing a slave is generally forbidden, but it is allowed when it makes a מצוה possible.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר holds keeping slaves is only optional
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that תנאים argue whether 'לעולם בהם תעבודו' is a רשות or a חובה. So maybe רבי אליעזר freed his slave simply because he holds it is optional, and his story proves nothing about a מצוה exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Of them you shall work forever' is optional. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: it is an obligation. So maybe רבי אליעזר holds like the one who says it is optional!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about the פסוק שמואל used. It then challenges the last answer: maybe רבי אליעזר is simply on the 'optional' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed that רבי אליעזר agreed it is forbidden to free a slave and only allowed it for a מצוה. But if רבי אליעזר holds like רבי ישמעאל that it is only a רשות, he could free a slave for any reason. Then his story would not show any exception to שמואל's rule.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Of them you shall work forever" is optional,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46. This is the same פסוק שמואל used in step 3.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is an obligation.
But perhaps Rabbi Eliezer holds
like the one who says it is optional!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the assumption behind step 5's answer that רבי אליעזר agrees freeing a slave is normally forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 5 that רבי אליעזר's story shows a מצוה exception to שמואל's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since there is a תנאים argument whether the פסוק is a רשות or a חובה, רבי אליעזר may hold it is a רשות. Then his action proves nothing about a מצוה exception.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי אליעזר holds it is an obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: a ברייתא says outright that רבי אליעזר holds 'לעולם בהם תעבודו' is a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, for it is taught clearly in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says it is an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting a ברייתא that states רבי אליעזר's opinion directly. He holds it is an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אליעזר holds keeping slaves is a חובה, he would normally forbid freeing them. So his freeing a slave to complete a מנין really does show the מצוה exception from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that keeping slaves is a חובה. Even so, he freed a slave to complete a מנין, so freeing a slave for a מצוה is an exception to שמואל's rule.

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind;
for it is taught explicitly:
Rabbi Eliezer says: it is an obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by quoting an explicit source for רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit source settles the תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבי אליעזר holds the פסוק is only a רשות.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds it is a חובה, so his story does prove the מצוה exception.

steps.title: Three habits that make homeowners lose their wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that homeowners lose their property through three habits: freeing their slaves, checking on their property on שבת, and holding their שבת meal during the time of the lecture in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Through these three things homeowners lose their property: that they free their slaves, that they inspect their property on שבת, and that they set their meals on שבת at the time of the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is freeing slaves, the גמרא brings a related saying of רבה. He lists three behaviors that cause people to lose their wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freeing slaves is now shown to be harmful in a practical way too, not only forbidden. The other two items also involve treating שבת wrongly: walking around your fields on שבת, and holding a meal at the time of the Torah lecture so that you miss it.

keyTerms.meaning: They go down, meaning they become poor
They inspect, they walk around to check
The study hall, where the Torah lecture is given

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Through these three things
homeowners go down from their property:
phrases.notes: Literally 'go down from their property', meaning they lose their wealth.

phrases.english: that they free their slaves,
and that they inspect their property on Shabbat,
and that they set their meals on Shabbat
at the time of the study hall.
phrases.notes: He means the time when the Torah lecture is being given, so they miss it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching connected by the shared topic of freeing slaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freeing slaves, inspecting property on שבת, and holding meals during the בית מדרש lecture cause homeowners to lose their wealth.

steps.title: Two families in ירושלים who were uprooted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells of two families in ירושלים. One held its meal on שבת and one held its meal on ערב שבת, and both families were destroyed. This supports רבה's third item.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There were two families in ירושלים. One set its meal on שבת and one set its meal on ערב שבת, and both of them were uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבה's point about badly timed שבת meals with a story from רבי יוחנן about two families who were destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family that held its meal on שבת matches רבה's case of eating during the lecture time. The גמרא does not spell out what was wrong with the meal on ערב שבת. It is commonly explained that eating a big meal then blurs the difference between ערב שבת and שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Set its meal, held a fixed meal

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
There were two families in Jerusalem,
one set its meal on Shabbat
and one set its meal on the eve of Shabbat,
and both of them were uprooted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third item in רבה's list.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that holding a שבת meal at the wrong time causes loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's account of two families in ירושלים who were uprooted.

steps.title: One who is מקדיש his slave sets him free
steps.stepSummary: רבה says in the name of רב: if a man declares his slave הקדש, the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said that רב said: One who is מקדיש his slave, the slave goes out to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about slaves. If an owner is מקדיש his slave, the slave becomes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because we might expect the slave to belong to the בית המקדש or that the owner owes his value. רב says instead that the result is freedom. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares something holy, given to the בית המקדש
He goes out to freedom, becomes a free man

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav said:
One who consecrates his slave, he goes out to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ עַבְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ruling about ways a slave can become free.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If an owner is מקדיש his slave, the slave becomes free.

steps.title: Why does this make the slave free?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking why being מקדיש a slave makes him free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner only said 'holy', not 'free'. So the גמרא needs to explain how those words lead to freedom.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being מקדיש a slave results in his freedom.

steps.title: He meant the slave should join the holy nation
steps.stepSummary: The slave's body cannot become holy, and the owner did not mention his value. So the owner must have meant that the slave should become part of the 'holy nation', a free Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: His body does not become holy. He did not say 'for his value'. So he meant that the slave should be part of the 'holy nation'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's ruling by ruling out the other things the owner could have meant. Only freedom is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot be offered or made holy like an animal, so the slave's body cannot become הקדש. The owner also did not say he is giving the slave's money value. The only meaning left is 'make him part of עם קדוש', which means setting him free as a full Jew.
steps.whatToRemember: Being מקדיש a slave frees him. His body cannot be holy, and the owner did not mention money, so his words must mean 'make him part of עם קדוש'.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the slave now belongs to the בית המקדש. רב's point is that the slave becomes a free man.

phrases.english: His body does not become holy;
for his value, he did not say;
he meant that he should be part of the "holy nation."

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפֵיהּ – לָא קַדִּישׁ; לִדְמֵי – לָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner's words must mean the slave should join עם קדוש, so he is freed, since the other meanings are impossible or were not said.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: renouncing ownership of a slave frees him
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes רב: if an owner makes his slave הפקר (gives up ownership), the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב: if someone gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רב said. This time it is about an owner who gives up ownership of his slave, not one who makes him holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבה quoted רב about הקדש. Here רב יוסף quotes רב about הפקר. A slave without an owner cannot stay a slave, so he becomes a free person.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives up ownership of something, making it ownerless
He goes out to freedom; he becomes a free person

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef says that Rav says:
One who renounces ownership of his slave, the slave goes free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב's ruling, alongside רבה's version from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner who makes his slave הפקר sets him free.

steps.title: How the two versions of רב's ruling relate
steps.stepSummary: The person who reports רב's ruling about הקדש would agree about הפקר even more. The person who reports it about הפקר might not agree about הקדש, because the owner may have meant only the slave's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the ruling was about making the slave holy, all the more so it applies to giving up ownership. According to the one who says it was about giving up ownership, it does not apply to making the slave holy, because perhaps the owner meant only the slave's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares רבה's version and רב יוסף's version. It shows how far each one reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even הקדש frees the slave, then giving up ownership completely surely does. But if רב only said this about הפקר, then הקדש may not free him. When an owner says 'he is holy,' he may simply mean his money value goes to the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; this case is even stronger
For its value; only the money it is worth

phrases.english: According to the one who says the ruling was about one who consecrates –
phrases.notes: This is רבה's version, from step 10.

phrases.english: all the more so one who renounces ownership;
according to the one who says the ruling was about one who renounces ownership –
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's version, from step 13.

phrases.english: but one who consecrates, no,
since perhaps he meant the slave's value.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מַקְדִּישׁ כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן מַפְקִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the difference in practice between the two versions of רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הקדש version includes הפקר. The הפקר version may leave out הקדש, because the owner may have meant only the slave's value.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב: הקדש frees the slave (רבה), or הפקר frees the slave (רב יוסף). The הקדש version is the broader one.

steps.title: Does the freed slave still need a document of release?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask whether a slave freed through הפקר or הקדש still needs a גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was raised: does he need a document of release, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. In these cases, is the slave fully free on his own, or does he still need a written document?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner never wrote a document. He only gave up ownership or made the slave holy. The question is whether that alone completes the freedom, or whether a גט שחרור is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked to them (the scholars)
A document of release that frees a slave

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ גֵּט שִׁיחְרוּר, אוֹ לֹא צָרִיךְ?
phrases.english: Does he need a document of release, or does he not need one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that the slave goes free and asks what is still needed to finish the process.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a slave freed by הפקר or הקדש still needs a גט שחרור.

steps.title: Both ways free the slave, but he needs a document
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין quotes רב: in both cases the slave goes free, but he still needs a גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב: in both this case and that case, the slave goes free, and he needs a document of release.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a direct quote from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב covers both cases together, הקדש and הפקר. The slave has a right to be free, but the freedom is only finished with a written גט שחרור. This quote also suggests that רב himself held both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Come and hear: for Rav Chiya bar Avin says that Rav says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה, יָצָא לְחֵירוּת,
phrases.english: in both this case and that case, the slave goes free,
phrases.notes: This means both the owner who makes him holy and the owner who gives up ownership.

phrases.english: and he needs a document of release.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. In both cases the slave goes free but still needs a גט שחרור.
steps.whatToRemember: A slave freed through הפקר or הקדש goes free, but he still needs a גט שחרור.

steps.title: A teaching that slaves made holy are not freed
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב's ruling from a ברייתא. It teaches that if slaves are among holy property, the treasurers may not free them. They must sell the slaves, and the buyers may free them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And we raised an objection to our teaching: if someone makes all his property holy and slaves were part of it, the treasurers may not free them. But they may sell them to others, and those others may free them. רבי says: I say that even the slave himself may pay his own value and go free, because it is as if the treasurer sold him to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רב's ruling that making a slave holy frees him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הקדש freed the slaves, there would be nothing left for the treasurers to sell. The ברייתא treats the slaves as holy property worth money, which the treasurers sell. Even רבי only lets the slave go free by paying for himself, not simply because he was made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: His own value; the price he is worth

phrases.english: Rabba said: And we raised an objection to our teaching –
phrases.notes: רבה is the one who reported רב's ruling about הקדש in step 10. Now he tells of a challenge raised against it.

phrases.english: one who makes his property holy, and there were slaves among it,
the treasurers are not allowed to set them free;
but they sell them to others,
and the others may set them free.
Rabbi says: I say,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא – נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי עַצְמוֹ וְיוֹצֵא,
phrases.english: even he, the slave himself, may give his own value and go free,
because it is as if the treasurer sold him to himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב's ruling about הקדש and attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that an owner who makes his slave הקדש sets him free.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats slaves made holy as property that the treasurers sell. That means הקדש did not free them.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not disagree that the slaves are still property. He only adds that the slave may be the 'buyer' and pay his own value. So both opinions in the ברייתא go against רב.

steps.title: רב has the standing of a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a ברייתא is no challenge to רב, because רב has the standing of a תנא and may disagree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you challenging רב from a ברייתא?! רב is a תנא, and he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge from the ברייתא without changing רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא. רב is special: he is counted like a תנא, so he may hold a different view. The ruling about הקדש stays standing as רב's own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים, here a ברייתא
You are throwing at; you are raising a challenge
A sage from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: Are you raising a ברייתא as a challenge against Rav?!
Rav is a תנא, and he disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Authority: רב has the standing of a תנא and may argue with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ברייתא should overturn the ruling of a later sage.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב may disagree with the ברייתא, so his ruling stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is used across ש״ס. רב, unlike other אמוראים, can be defended by saying he is a תנא and may argue.

steps.title: A challenge from a פסוק about holy things that cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a דרשה on the פסוק 'אך כל חרם... מאדם'. It explains 'מאדם' as a person's Canaanite slaves, so slaves can become חרם and stay property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'But every devoted thing... of man' — these are his Canaanite slaves and maidservants!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב. This one is a teaching built on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a person who devotes his property, including 'of man.' The teaching says this means his slaves. So a slave can be devoted and stay property, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Something devoted, given over for holy use

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"But every devoted thing, etc., of man" –
these are his Canaanite slaves and maidservants!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was set aside, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a teaching on a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that making a slave holy sets him free.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching says slaves can be devoted as holy property. That means devoting them does not free them.

steps.title: The teaching speaks about devoting only the slave's value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching speaks about an owner who said he was devoting only the slave's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he said he was devoting the slave's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case the teaching speaks about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner clearly says 'for his value,' then the slave's money worth goes to holy use, and the slave stays property to be sold. רב's ruling is about a plain 'he is holy,' which is understood as making him part of the 'holy nation,' as in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A formula that narrows a source to a specific case

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
Where he said it was for the slave's value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the source speaks about devoting only the slave's value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to say any devoting of a slave leaves him as property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only when the owner says 'for his value' does the slave stay property. A plain declaration of הקדש still frees him, as רב said.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling stands. A plain declaration of הקדש frees the slave, but saying 'for his value' does not. In either case of freedom, a גט שחרור is still needed.

steps.title: Why not explain the other ברייתא the same way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if one source can be explained as devoting only the slave's value, why not explain the treasurers' ברייתא that way too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then let us also say the other ברייתא is talking about someone who said he devotes the slave's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own earlier answer. If 'only his value' works for the פסוק teaching in step 20, it should also work for the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא defended רב by saying he is a תנא and may disagree with a ברייתא. That is a strong move. If the simpler answer of 'only his value' works, the גמרא would not need it, so why not use the simpler answer here too?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
For his value (only his money worth)

phrases.english: If so, the other one also
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the ברייתא about the treasurers from step 17.

phrases.english: is where he said 'for his value'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אִידַּךְ נָמֵי דְּאָמַר לִדְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 20 and asks why it was not also used for the ברייתא of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 18 (that רב is a תנא and may disagree)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'only his value' resolves one source, the same answer should resolve the treasurers' ברייתא, so step 18's bigger move would be unneeded.

steps.title: The treasurers would have no role
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא talks about the treasurers. That only makes sense if the slave himself became holy property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then the ברייתא says 'the treasurers may not free them.' What do the treasurers have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the treasurers' ברייתא cannot be about devoting only the value. Its own wording does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner devoted only the slave's value, the slave never belonged to הקדש, and he still belongs to his owner. Then the treasurers would have no power over him at all. Telling them they 'may not free him' only makes sense if the slave himself is holy property in their hands.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurers in charge of holy property (הקדש)
What do they have to do with it?

phrases.english: If so,
'The treasurers are not allowed'
'to set them free' —
treasurers, what do they have to do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by showing the ברייתא's wording rules out the 'only his value' reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording of the source proves the case cannot be 'only his value'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The treasurers' ברייתא could be explained as devoting only the value, like the פסוק teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mention of the treasurers shows the slave himself was holy, so the only way to defend רב is that he is a תנא.

steps.title: The 'others' would have no role either
steps.stepSummary: A second proof: the ברייתא says the slaves are sold to others who then free them. That also assumes the slave himself was holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: 'But they sell them to others, and the others free them.' What do the others have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why the ברייתא cannot be about devoting only the value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slave stayed with his original owner, the treasurers could not sell him, and no buyer could gain the right to free him. A sale from הקדש to buyers only makes sense if הקדש owned the slave himself.

phrases.english: And further — 'But they sell them to others,'
'and the others set them free' —
others, what do they have to do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second wording proof to the answer of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps only the mention of the treasurers is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sale to buyers also shows that הקדש owned the slave himself.

steps.title: רבי's words 'as if he sold him to himself'
steps.stepSummary: A third proof: רבי says the slave can pay his own value because it is as if הקדש sold him to himself. That only fits if הקדש owned him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: 'רבי says: I say that even he himself gives his own value and goes free, because it is as if he sold him to himself.' And if it was only his value, what does 'because it is as if he sold him to himself' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof from the end of the same ברייתא. With this, it finishes showing that the ברייתא is about the slave himself becoming holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי pictures the treasurer selling the slave to the slave himself. You can only sell something you own. So הקדש must own the slave, and the 'only his value' reading cannot work. That is why step 18 had to say רב, as a תנא, disagrees with this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: As if he sells him to himself

steps.whatToRemember: Three parts of the treasurers' ברייתא (the treasurers, the buyers, and רבי's 'as if he sold him to himself') all show the slave himself became holy. So the ברייתא really argues with רב, and רב is defended only because he is a תנא.

phrases.english: And further — 'רבי says: I say,'

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא – נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי עַצְמוֹ וְיוֹצֵא,
phrases.english: 'even he himself gives his own value and goes free,'
phrases.notes: 'He' is the slave himself. He can pay הקדש his worth, the way a buyer would.

phrases.english: 'because it is as if he sells him to himself' —
and if it was only for his value,
what is 'because it is as if he sells him to himself'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לִדְמֵי, מַאי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹכְרוֹ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and final wording proof, finishing the answer to step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional wording proof that completes the answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the ברייתא could still be stretched to mean only the value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא clearly treats the slave himself as holy, so the defense of רב in step 18 is necessary.

steps.title: A new challenge: the devoted slave keeps working
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone who devotes his slave has devoted only his value, and the slave keeps working and being fed. This suggests the slave does not go free, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who devotes his slave, the slave works and eats, because he devoted only his value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge to רב's ruling from step 10, that one who is מקדיש his slave sets him free, this time from another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a devoted slave goes free (with a גט שחרור). This ברייתא says plainly that devoting a slave means devoting only his money worth. The slave just keeps working and being fed as before, which shows he does not go free.

keyTerms.meaning: One who devotes something to הקדש

phrases.english: Come and hear: One who devotes his slave —
he works and eats,
because he devoted only his value!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with the treasurers' ברייתא, the גמרא brings a new source against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling in step 10 that a devoted slave goes free
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says any devotion of a slave is only of his value and the slave keeps working, so he does not go free.
